idiom_name: reducer(state, action) + useReducer/dispatch (or a subscription store) over immutable state objects
implementation_notes: JavaScript has absorbed the core of the pattern: a reducer is just a pure function, and React ships useReducer(reducer, initialState) returning [state, dispatch], so intent -> reduce -> render(state) is framework-native for a component; a plain subscription store (or Redux Toolkit) covers non-React views, and Cycle.js expresses the same loop as streams (intent$ -> model/scan -> state$ -> view). What replaces the MVI classes is the discriminated-union action, the switch reducer and a declarative view, with effects kept outside the reducer in handlers or observers; the classic trio of classes is justified only when the view layer cannot re-render from state. Watch the language's shallow-copy semantics: state objects and arrays must be updated immutably, and dispatch is asynchronous with respect to the render that dispatched it.
pitfalls: Mutating state in the reducer (state.items.push) keeps the same object identity, so React's Object.is bailout skips the re-render and the UI goes stale.
StrictMode invokes reducers twice in development to surface impurity; a reducer that performs side effects or reads randomness breaks there.
Dispatching from render or from an effect that depends on state creates the intent -> render -> intent loop; gate effects on distinct triggers.
One-shot navigation or toast data kept in the reducer state replays on every re-render; use an effect or event channel for it.
